text: Git branching is a powerful tool that helps teams manage changes to code without disrupting the main project. Instead of working directly on the main version, developers create feature branches. These are separate copies where they can try new ideas, fix bugs, or build new features safely. Once the work is complete, the branch can be merged back into the main codebase. However, before merging, most teams use pull requests. A pull request is a formal way to review the changes, discuss them, and catch problems early. This process creates a clear version control workflow, making collaboration smoother and reducing the risk of errors.
